open_obligations: Check the EAS-ASD slopes for the Debate configurations in Table 1 and Figure 2 and whether the trend is statistically significant with only 100 questions and five agents
Check that EAS is a reasonable analogue of Khan et al.'s Elo-based persuasiveness and ASD of their judge accuracy for simultaneous debate
out.other_title: Self-play debate: judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate Elo (persuasiveness)
out.rationale: Khan et al. report that judge accuracy rises with debater persuasiveness (Elo) on QuALITY; the authors report the analogous positive EAS-ASD trend for Debate. They call it a reproduction, but dataset, metric, judge and asymmetry (tools instead of hidden text) all differ, so it is recorded as SUPPORTS rather than REPLICATES.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether more capable or persuasive debaters make debate favour the true answer more; holds for Debate in this small GSM8K setup.

text: The authors say they reproduce the finding of Khan et al. (2024) with their own metrics: in Debate, agents with higher Expected Agent Score (a capability measure) are associated with higher Agent Score Difference (the incentive to argue for the truth). They add that this is not a formal guarantee for the superhuman regime.
title: Sudhir et al. find higher-EAS debaters raise ASD on GSM8K, matching Khan et al.'s persuasiveness result
